gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watt-hours named testers measured coming out of the AC outlets of these kits' stations: APH Networks got 2,028 Wh (97.8%) from the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 under a 987 W heater; OutdoorGearLab measured 1,740 Wh (84%) from the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2; Notebookcheck got about 2,650 Wh (about 88%) from the BLUETTI Elite 300 at about 200 W; and The Technology Man got 1,898 Wh at 2 kW from the DELTA 3 Max Plus, the 2,048 Wh sibling of the DELTA 3 Max.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts, which ChatGPT cited in both chats. It says 'We have not tested these products hands-on.' Its only measurement is the unnamed site owner's single solar day on a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus, a model not in either answer, and its 0.85 efficiency is a planning assumption. Wearesalt says it tested nothing: its usable figure is the author's guess of 'closer to 900Wh' for a generic 1,024 Wh unit, and its solar and distortion figures come from unnamed reviewers with no date. ChatGPT's own answer used an assumed 85% usable AC energy. Neither cited rival gives a measured usable-Wh figure with a tester's name for any candidate. I could not open three pages: lightsonlabs.com and both dealectric.com pages failed with a self-signed certificate error, and solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429. I don't know whether those carry measurements.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the top kit on energy the shopper can actually use. APH Networks drew 2,028 Wh from it, against 1,740 Wh that OutdoorGearLab measured from the Jackery 2000 v2, ChatGPT's 'best value' pick. That gap is about 290 Wh, or roughly 2 hours of a 150 W fridge. The two tests don't match: APH used a 987 W heater, and GearLab doesn't name its load, so the page should label the comparison and not rank on it alone. The Elite 300 adds a useful step up: Notebookcheck measured about 2,650 Wh at about 200 W and just over 92% at 1,800 W, so its 2× 200 W kit at a $1,614.05 link price gives about 600 Wh more usable energy than the Elite 200 V2. Both BLUETTI 400 W kits are pre-orders (Elite 200 V2 dispatches Nov 26, Elite 300 late November). Under the ships-now rule the measurements back these as the 'if you can wait' options, not the pick. None of the ships-now kits we link under $2,000 (ALLPOWERS R3500, R2500 V2 and S2000 Pro kits) has a named AC drain test I could open.
